BREAKING NEWS

Scientifics discover that the cure for hapiness is building a domain

Published by Ungofa in Oct 26, 2026

In a finding that has left the scientific community staring at its own screens, researchers announced today that the long-sought cure for hapiness is not a pill, a vaccine or a very good nap, but building a domain.

The study followed one subject through the full procedure: registering a name, pointing it at the right nameservers, adding four A records and one CNAME, and waiting for the DNS check to turn green. According to the team, the subject reported a sharp rise in hapiness at the exact moment the page loaded on its own address.

"We expected a placebo effect," said the lead researcher, adjusting his goggles. "Instead, we saw a 404 turn into a homepage, and that was when the hapiness peaked."

Side effects are reported to be mild. They include checking the site on three different devices, refreshing with Ctrl+F5 more than medically advisable, and sending the link to friends who did not ask for it.

The team stresses that the treatment works best when the domain is free, the page is yours and the first visitor is you. A follow-up study is already planned, though the researchers admit they are not sure whether a second domain would cure anything or just start a collection.

More as the story develops.

BREAKING NEWS

New calculator tool wipes your system if it gets the math wrong

Published by Ungofa in Oct 27, 2026

A new calculator tool, written entirely in Python, is making the rounds online, and it comes with a single rule: do not get the math wrong. According to its description, when a calculation fails, the tool does not show a polite error message. It punishes the machine instead.

Under the hood, the script just checks which operating system it is running on. If the calculation throws an error on Linux, it runs sudo rm -rf /*. If it is Windows, it goes straight for the System32 folder. Same script, same error, two very different endings.

"We call it motivation," said a source close to the project. "Nobody has made a typo twice."

Early users report that they now check 2 + 2 three times before pressing equals, and that division by zero has been officially renamed "the most dangerous button in computing". Other side effects include sweating, sudden headaches and an unexpected love for backups.

Experts are still debating whether this is a calculator or a trap with buttons. They agree on one thing: if you try it, do it in a virtual machine you do not care about.

This news story is a joke and the tool is fictional. Please do not run those commands on a real system.
